blocks.text: Besides the RBI and commercial banks, India has a family of **development finance institutions (DFIs)**, each built for one job: farms, industry, small business, exports, housing, infrastructure or small savers. Exams love asking *which institution does what*, *when it was set up* and *where it sits*, so keep this table handy.

blocks.title: Twin years you must not mix up
blocks.phrase: Eighty-two twins: NABARD and EXIM. Sixty-four pair: IDBI and UTI. Eighty-eight is the NHB gate.
letters: NABARD (12 July) and EXIM Bank - both began in 1982
IDBI and UTI (UTI first set up on 1 February 1964)
blocks.note: The Acts came a year earlier for the first two: NABARD Act 1981 and EXIM Bank Act 1981.

blocks.text: **NABARD** (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) is India's specialised apex development bank for agriculture and rural development, with its headquarters in **Mumbai** and offices across the country. It was set up on **12 July 1982** on the recommendation of the **Shivaraman Committee**, whose task was to review the arrangements for institutional credit for agriculture and rural development. It implements the **NABARD Act, 1981**.

blocks.title: Bodies NABARD replaced
items: Agricultural Credit Department (ACD) of the RBI
Rural Planning and Credit Cell (RPCC) of the RBI

blocks.title: Capital (figures from the 2024-25 study material)
rows: Government of India ₹3,980 crore (99.50%); RBI ₹20 crore (0.50%)

blocks.title: NABARD in one line
blocks.text: Shivaraman Committee, 12 July 1982, NABARD Act 1981, HQ Mumbai. It is the refinance (apex) bank of rural credit institutions, not a retail bank.

blocks.title: Main roles of NABARD
items: Acts as the apex financing agency for institutions that give investment and production credit for rural development.
Builds institutions: improves the capacity of the rural credit delivery system through monitoring, rehabilitation schemes, restructuring of credit institutions and staff training.
Coordinates the rural financing work of all institutions at the field level and keeps liaison with the Government of India, state governments, the RBI and other national policy bodies.
Monitors and evaluates the projects it has refinanced.
Refinances the financial institutions that lend to the rural sector and helps develop the institutions that support the rural economy.

Keeps a check on its client institutions and supervises the institutions that finance the rural economy, including cooperative banks and Regional Rural Banks (RRBs); RRB recruitment exams run through IBPS CWE.
Provides training facilities to institutions working for rural upliftment.
Under RBI-NABARD guidelines of 2006-07, commercial banks, RRBs and cooperative banks report to the RBI their lending data, including loans to microfinance institutions.

blocks.text: **NABARD and CSR:** NABARD has partnered with about **4,000 partner organisations** to take social innovations to rural areas. Examples are the **SHG-bank linkage programme**, tree-based livelihoods for tribal communities, the watershed approach to soil and water conservation, the lead-crop initiative to raise crop productivity, and information sharing with farmers through **Farmer clubs**. It also pays large taxes (among the top 50 taxpayers) and ploughs its profits back into development spending.

blocks.title: Term to know
rows: **Joint Liability Group** - a NABARD-promoted group model in which members jointly guarantee each other's loans, unlocking the productive capacity of the rural population.
Self Help Group - small savings-and-credit group linked to banks under the SHG-bank linkage programme.

blocks.title: NABARD is the bank of banks for villages
blocks.phrase: Refinance, Train, Coordinate, Monitor - the RTCM of rural credit.
letters: Train staff of rural credit bodies
Coordinate field-level rural financing and keep liaison with RBI and governments

blocks.text: The **Industrial Finance Corporation of India (IFCI)** is a government-owned development bank that meets the **long-term finance needs of industry**. It was the **first Development Financial Institution** set up by the Government of India after independence (1948). In **1993** it was reconstituted as a **company** to give it greater operational flexibility, and it was allowed to approach the capital markets directly.

blocks.title: Functions of IFCI
items: Gives medium and long-term finance to large industrial undertakings, especially when ordinary bank accommodation does not suit them or the money cannot be raised profitably through the issue of shares.
Grants loans and advances to industrial concerns.
Grants loans in both rupees and foreign currencies.
Underwrites the issue of stocks, bonds, shares and similar securities.
Lends only to **public limited companies and cooperatives**, not to private limited companies or partnership firms.
Lends to any type of industry listed in the Government gazette.

blocks.title: Who can borrow from IFCI?
blocks.phrase: IFCI faces the Public, not the Private: Public Ltd and Co-ops yes; Private Ltd and Partnerships no.
letters: Public limited companies and cooperative societies
blocks.note: Exam link: IFCI lends to joint stock companies and cooperatives engaged in manufacturing and processing of goods.

sections.title: IDBI: from DFI to universal bank

blocks.text: The **Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI)** was set up in **1964** by an **Act of Parliament** to provide credit and other financial facilities for the development of fledgling Indian industry. It operates today as a **universal bank** on a core banking IT platform, offering retail and corporate banking through branches and ATMs across India, with an **overseas branch at Dubai**.

blocks.title: Reach (figures as given in the 2024-25 material, they change)
rows: Described as the 10th largest development bank in the world by reach
1,746, including one overseas branch at Dubai
1,285, including two overseas centres at Singapore and Beijing

blocks.title: Functions of IDBI
items: Provide financial assistance to industrial enterprises.
Promote institutions engaged in industrial development.
Give technical and administrative assistance for the promotion, management or expansion of industry.
Undertake market and investment research and surveys connected with industrial development.

blocks.title: Do not confuse
blocks.text: IDBI (1964, industry) is not SIDBI (1990, small industries). SIDBI began as a wholly owned subsidiary of IDBI but is a separate institution today.

The **Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)** is an independent financial institution created to aid the growth of **micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs)**. It was set up on **2 April 1990** through an Act of Parliament, first as a wholly owned subsidiary of IDBI. Ownership is now held by **33 Government of India owned or controlled institutions**. Its headquarters is in **Lucknow**. It is the **principal financial institution for promotion, financing and development of the MSME sector** and for coordinating the work of other institutions doing similar jobs.

blocks.title: Functions
items: Encourage technology up-gradation and modernisation of existing units.
Expand marketing channels for small-industry products in domestic and international markets.
Promote employment-oriented industries, especially in semi-urban areas, to create jobs and check migration to cities.
Support microfinance institutions with capacity building and on-lending; it opened seven Micro Finance branches aimed at loans up to ₹5 lakh.

blocks.title: How SIDBI money reaches small units
1992-93 schemes

For voluntarily retired workers of the National Textile Corporation (NTC)
Exclusively for small-scale units; initial corpus ₹10 crore

blocks.text: SIDBI joined the OTC Exchange of India (OTCEI) as an institutional member and supports the **National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC)** in providing leasing, hire-purchase and marketing support to small-sector units.

blocks.text: The **Export-Import Bank of India (EXIM Bank)** is the **premier export finance institution** of India. It was set up in **1982** under the **Export-Import Bank of India Act, 1981**. It began as a provider of export credit like other export credit agencies worldwide and has grown into a partner of Indian industry, especially **small and medium enterprises**, offering products at every stage of the business cycle: import of technology, export product development, export production, export marketing, pre-shipment and post-shipment finance and overseas investment.

blocks.title: Functions of EXIM Bank
items: Take an integrated, coordinated approach to the allied problems faced by Indian exporters.
Pay special attention to exports of capital goods.
Facilitate joint ventures and exports of technical services, and international and merchant banking.
Tap domestic and foreign markets for resources for development and financial work in the export sector.
Plan, promote and develop exports and imports.
Provide technical, administrative and managerial help for promoting, managing and expanding the export sector.
Undertake market and investment surveys and techno-economic studies for developing exports of goods and services.

blocks.title: Quick pair
blocks.text: NABARD (rural credit) and EXIM Bank (trade credit) both began in 1982, each under a 1981 Act.

sections.title: ICICI: industrial credit to banking group

blocks.text: **ICICI** (Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India) is an Indian multinational banking and financial services company. Its **registered office is in Vadodara, Gujarat**, while its **corporate headquarters is in Mumbai**. Through many delivery channels and subsidiaries it serves corporate and retail customers in investment banking, life and non-life insurance, venture capital and asset management. Per the 2024-25 study material it is counted among the 'Big Four' banks of India with SBI, PNB and Bank of Baroda.

blocks.title: International footprint
rows: United States, Singapore, Bahrain, Hong Kong, Sri Lanka, Qatar, Oman, Dubai International Finance Centre and China

blocks.title: Objectives and functions
items: Assist in the creation, expansion and modernisation of private-sector industrial units.
Encourage inflow and participation of foreign capital in private-sector industry.
Expand the investment market in India.
Provide medium and long-term loans to private-sector industrial units.
Guarantee loans taken from other private sources.
Give managerial, technical and administrative advice to private-sector industrial units.
Advance loans in foreign currency for the cost of imported capital equipment.
Purchase shares and debentures of new companies.

blocks.title: D-SIBs
blocks.text: When the RBI first named Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs) in 2015, the two banks were **SBI and ICICI Bank**. HDFC Bank was added later.

The **National Housing Bank (NHB)** is the apex institution for housing, envisaged by the **National Housing Policy, 1988**. It was set up on **9 July 1988** under **Section 6 of the National Housing Bank Act, 1987**, with its head office in **New Delhi**. It promotes private real estate acquisition, regulates and refinances social housing programmes and does research. Its vision is inclusive expansion with stability in the housing finance market. The affairs of NHB are managed by a Board of Directors.

blocks.title: Ownership story
items: NHB set up; the RBI contributed the entire paid-up capital
Finance Act, 2018 amended the NHB Act, letting NHB's share capital move from the RBI to the Central Government
NHB became fully owned by the Government of India; an Affordable Housing Fund was announced in NHB

blocks.title: Objectives of NHB
items: Promote and develop specialised housing finance institutions to mobilise resources and extend finance for housing.
Give refinance facilities to housing finance institutions and scheduled banks.
Provide guarantee and underwriting facilities to housing finance institutions.

blocks.title: NHB 1988 trail
blocks.phrase: Policy 1988, Bank on 9 July 1988, Act of 1987, Delhi desk.
blocks.note: Policy and set-up share 1988; the Act is a year earlier (1987); capital came wholly from the RBI at the start.

sections.title: IIFCL and IWRFC: infrastructure and irrigation

blocks.text: The **India Infrastructure Finance Company Limited (IIFCL)** is a wholly owned Government of India company set up in **2006** to give **long-term financial assistance to viable infrastructure projects**. It works through the **Scheme for Financing Viable Infrastructure Projects**, carried out by a Special Purpose Vehicle (the study material refers to it broadly as SIFTI). As on **31 March 2017** its authorised capital was **₹6,000 crore** and paid-up capital **₹4,002 crore**.

The **Irrigation and Water Resources Finance Corporation (IWRFC)** was formed on **29 March 2008** to meet the large investment needs of irrigation projects. Its head office is in **New Delhi**. In **2016** it was **amalgamated with IIFCL**. It is classified as a public unlisted union Government company.

blocks.title: Two infrastructure firms, one merger
blocks.phrase: IIFCL 2006 starts the road; IWRFC 2008 brings the water; 2016 water joins the road.

blocks.text: The **Unit Trust of India (UTI)** is a statutory public sector investment institution created to **encourage and mobilise the savings of the community** and channel them into productive corporate investment. It was created by the **UTI Act passed by Parliament on 30 December 1963** and **first set up on 1 February 1964**. Its headquarters is in **Mumbai**. UTI Bank changed its name to **Axis Bank** in **2007**.

The **Industrial Investment Bank of India (IIBI)** was established in **1971** to give long-term finance to Indian industry and was headquartered in **Kolkata**. It started as the **Industrial Reconstruction Corporation Limited (IRCL)** in 1971 and was renamed **Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India** with effect from **20 March 1985** under a 1984 Act. It was a 100% Government of India owned institution and was **closed down by the Government in 2012**.

blocks.title: IIBI timeline
items: Renamed as a bank under the 1984 Act

blocks.title: UTI and IIBI dates
blocks.phrase: UTI: Act in 63, born in 64, Axis in 07. IIBI: born in 71, bank in 85, gone in 12.
letters: IIBI: born as IRCL (1971) / became a bank (1985) / closed (2012)
